description: Standing Capability Ledger for this repository. Written by the human on approving escalation D-001 (2026-09-10), corrected 2026-09-11 to withdraw the updateDebugScreenshotTest grant. Standing = per-repository toolchain that survives this goal and future runs. The runtime reads only the 'allow' arrays, verbatim.

entries.intent: Build, unit-test and lint the app so task completion can be evidenced (ENGINE.md §10). Nothing in this repository has been built by the engine yet; without this, no task can ever be marked complete. Includes the dependency resolution Gradle performs as part of these tasks.

Verify rendered UI against the recorded reference images, so acceptance criteria about appearance, contrast and layout are provable by command output instead of being narrowed away or escalated. Host-side (layoutlib on the JVM) - no emulator, no device, no adb.

entries._withheld: updateDebugScreenshotTest is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from this ledger.
entries._why: It overwrites the committed reference images. An engine holding it, facing a red screenshot test, has a one-command route to making the failure disappear by re-recording wrong output as correct - the same class of act as editing an approved DoD. The android-compose-visual-testing stack pack withholds it on purpose and calls the asymmetry the most important line in the pack; the 2026-09-10 D-001 approval granted it standing anyway, which is the error this entry exists to prevent recurring.
entries._how_to_grant: When a baseline genuinely must move - an intentional UI change, or a new state that has no reference yet - the engine raises an Escalation Request and the human adds a GOAL-SCOPED entry to .ai/capabilities.json (not here), which expires with the run. Recording a new reference is the safe half; overwriting a currently-failing one is not, and the permission matcher cannot tell them apart, so a human sits at that grant.
entries.intent: placeholder - no capability is granted by this entry

Read files out of earlier commits and out of a prior run's Loop Branch. Bash(git show*) is already baseline, but on Windows/Git Bash MSYS rewrites 'ref:path' into 'ref;path' and the command fails for exactly the paths that matter (.ai/**, knowledge/**). MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 is the documented workaround, and the leading assignment means the baseline rule does not match it.
